chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jabalah, from Dharīḥ, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and informed him of the times of salat (prayer). He said: 'Perform salat al-fajr when the dawn breaks; perform the first prayer when the sun declines; perform salat al-ʿaṣr shortly after it; perform salat al-maghrib when the disc sets; and perform salat al-ʿatamah when the twilight disappears.' Then he came to him the next day and said: 'Delay al-fajr until there is brightness,' so he delayed it. Then he delayed al-ẓuhr until it was the time in which he had performed al-ʿaṣr, and he performed al-ʿaṣr shortly after it, and he performed al-maghrib before the twilight disappeared, and he performed al-ʿatamah when a third of the night had passed. Then he said: 'What is between these two times is a time, and the best of the time is its beginning.'
Then he عليه السلام said: 'The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: Were it not that I dislike causing hardship for my Ummah, I would have delayed it until midnight.'

And he said: I said to him, 'Some people among the companions of Abī al-Khaṭṭāb delay al-maghrib until the stars become intertwined.' He said: So he replied, 'I declare myself free before Allah from whoever does this deliberately.'

key_terms.أَفْضَلُ: most excellent, indicating the superiority of praying at the earliest time
key_terms.الشَّفَقُ: the twilight whose disappearance marks the time of ʿishāʾ
key_terms.الْعَصْرَ: the afternoon prayer performed after ẓuhr
key_terms.الْفَجْرَ: the dawn prayer and its beginning time
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبَ: the sunset prayer beginning with the setting of the disc
key_terms.زَالَتِ: the sun's decline from the zenith, marking the start of ẓuhr
key_terms.مَوَاقِيتَ: the appointed times of the obligatory salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the times of the daily salat and the ruling on delaying maghrib?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the prescribed time ranges for the daily salat (prayer), showing both the earliest and later portions of their valid times. It also states that the most excellent time is the beginning of the prayer time, while condemning the deliberate delay of al-maghrib beyond its proper time.
